name: 1905 Prairie Avenue — the Marshall Field house (Second Empire)

grade.why: Pictured: 16 of the pictures on the Images tab show it.

documented_range.note: The 1904 target to the 1911 sheet that draws the house: the T-1841 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped), and the 1893 Pictorial Chicago plate shows the house standing before the target. Its building and loss dates are the register's (1871-1873; lost 1955) and are not read here.

placement.position_note: The rear corner of the main body's rectangle (lot frame u 24.250, v -14.250 m from the middle of the rear lot line), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the georeference's independent check is 1.47 m RMS. Rotation 179.444 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line. Kept from the district draft (T-2330) by T-3260: the plate does not move it.
placement.symbolic_location: 1905 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1905 (data/street_grid/1904.json), east side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 18th to 20th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 28).

footprint.note: The main body in the house's frame (u toward Prairie Avenue, west, from the rear wall; v south from the north wall): the front at u 21.0, the depth the 1911 sheet's trace (s28fp-1905-b1 p1). T-3271: the front runs 16.8 m, Hunt's written 55 ft 0 in over all on his plan of the principal floor (hunt_field_1905_principal_floor_plan), not the sheet's 15.25 m: the 923 Prairie photograph and the Daily News negative DN-0003324 fit that plan (3.0 and 1.6 px RMS) and cannot be fitted to the sheet's front. The north wall stays where the sheet and the district draft put it and the extra 1.55 m is laid at the south, as both photographs' cameras read the canted corner and the south flank about 1.5 m south of the sheet's (the sheet's 50-foot scale and its trace carry about that much). The sheet's two rear pieces stand on it as K01 rear wings and its south-flank bulge as the conservatory's bow (bays). The plate cuts the south-west corner on a canted face that the sheet draws square; the cut stands on this rectangle as cant_corner (T-3261).

stories.note: Two storeys of brick over a raised stone basement, under a mansard: the plate's walls stop at a bracketed cornice over the second storey and the roof's steep slated faces rise over it with dormers. The 1911 sheet's '3S.B.' counts the mansard's attic as its third storey, as it does at 1816.

construction.note: The sheet colours the house as brick; the plate shows brick walls (dark) dressed in light stone: the basement, the belts, the window surrounds, the frieze and the corner strips.

principal_floor_m.note: T-3271: the water table under the principal storey about 2.0 m over the walk, read through the 923 Prairie photograph's camera, which is fitted to Hunt's plan of the principal floor (data/reference_views/marshall_field_house_1905_prairie/chicagology_923_photo.json). The 1893 plate's camera had read 2.2 m with the heights held, not read.

storey_heights_m.note: T-3271: read through the 923 Prairie photograph's camera, fitted to Hunt's plan of the principal floor (data/reference_views/marshall_field_house_1905_prairie/chicagology_923_photo.json): the stone belt at the chamber floor about 6.1 m over grade and the frieze's foot about 9.6 m, so a 4.1 m principal storey and a 4.0 m chamber storey to the wall head, the 0.5 m frieze (wall_head) standing inside its top from 9.6 m. The Daily News view, its heights left free, reads the brick lower still (about 6.9 m from the water table); the two disagree by under a metre and the fitted camera is followed. Before: 5.2 and 4.2 m, read through the 1893 plate's camera with the heights held at 2.2 and 11.6 m, which set the cornice about 1.5-1.8 m too high.

service_wall_brick.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the K03 common brick panel 1620 wears; the print is monochrome.

roof_pitch_deg.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the mansard's upper deck at 10 degrees, as 1620's; the photograph shows only its cresting.

stair_tread_m.note: RECONSTRUCTED: 0.3 m treads, as 1620's; the photograph's flight is half hidden by its cheek and the fence.

rainwater.note: RECONSTRUCTED: K04 half-round copper gutters and round pipes to splash stones, as 1620's.

window_kit.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the K06 two-over-two flat sash and area lights 1620 wears; the photograph shows two-over-two sash in the principal windows. T-3271: the round-headed basement lights (the plate, the engraving and the 923 Prairie photograph) take K06's fixed round-headed basement light, as 1811's do; their bars are not modelled.

street_front_trim.note: Every window of the plate's front stands in a light stone surround under a moulded head with a cornice: K09's lintel with a cornice hood on both storeys. T-3270: the chamber windows' heads carry the plate's carved crests, a palmette between two scroll volutes standing on each hood and stopping under the frieze (1.3 m across, 0.3 m high); and the frieze carries the plate's pairs of carved rings (its '1 O O 1', the cornice's paired brackets standing for its upright strokes) in the four bracket bays the crests leave clear: the north end, both sides of the pier between the north and door columns, and the pier between the narrow and wide columns. The kit's evenly spaced bracket pairs stand over the piers where the plate's stand at the columns' edges. T-3271: re-laid on the re-read front's bracket bays (stations 1.58 m apart from 0.2 m), centred 0.99, 4.16, 5.74, 8.91 and 12.08 m along it and 0.48 m under the wall head as before; the longer front gives the door and narrow columns' pier a bay of its own, so it carries its pair as the plate's every pier does. The principal windows' heads, under the balconies' slabs and consoles, keep the kit's plain hood. RECONSTRUCTED: the crests' and rings' carving is the kit's simple palmette, volutes and rings, not the plate's leafwork, which its halftone does not resolve (L-field-1905-carving-3270).

street_front_iron.note: T-3261: the plate's three iron balconies on the front, read against its window columns: one before the chamber window of the north column, one before the door column's (over the door) and one before the wide column's, none before the narrow column's. Each stands on the stone belt at the chamber floor (2.0 + 4.1 = 6.1 m, T-3271) on two scrolled stone consoles, its guard about 0.9 m high before a chamber light that runs down behind it to a sill 0.3 m over the floor. Lengths from the plate's pixels scaled by the column spacing (47-52 px a metre locally): the north one about 2.3 m, the door column's about 3.5 m, the wide column's about 2.5 m, each centred on its window (their fronts read north of the windows only by the oblique view's parallax); T-3270: the door column's is built at the plate's 3.5 m, centred on its window (5.9-9.4 m since T-3271), on the plate's tall scrolled consoles, run 0.9 m down the wall beside the door's surround. About 0.7 m proud and the slab 0.2 m deep, inferred from the plate's consoles. The undated photograph from the west side of the avenue (chicagology_1905_field_photo, cross-check only, not a source of this) shows the same three and the narrow column without one. The pierced panels' scroll pattern is the kit's, RECONSTRUCTED. T-3271: with the front re-read to Hunt's 16.8 m and the cut to 2.15 m, each is laid centred on its column's new place (the north one 2.0-4.4 m, the wide one 12.05-14.45 m, 2.4 m long and 0.2 m short of the cut), so the wide column's runs its plate length where it had been stopped at 1.9 m. T-3271 (the sign-off): the south flank's two chamber balconies the 923 Prairie photograph shows (the 1893 plate and the engraving show the first): before the chamber window of the column just behind the canted corner (3.1 m back) and before the one about 14.7 m back, each the front's kind on two consoles on the chamber floor's belt, 1.4 m long centred on its window, 0.5 m proud (read shallower than the front's in the photograph). The chamber window over the conservatory at 9.2 m stands behind the conservatory's own railed deck, which is the iron the photograph shows before it.

wall_head.note: The plate's wall head: a deep cornice on paired brackets over a frieze about 0.7 m high, built 0.5 m to leave the chamber heads room under it (its roundels and the carved blocks over the window columns are not modelled), as 1900's K10 bracketed cornice.

roof_form.note: The plate's slated mansard, steep faces over the cornice with dormers in them and an iron cresting along its curb.

eave_overhang_m.note: The cornice's projection, read against the brackets' depth in the plate.

mansard.note: A tall slated mansard over the cornice, its curb about 5 m over the cornice's top through its camera (data/reference_views/marshall_field_house_1905_prairie/pictorial_1893_plate.json), built at 4.5 m, the K05 contract's ceiling for a face holding one storey (the plate's further half metre is an open difference in the match record), its faces steep. Dormers where the plate shows them: three on the street face over the north window column, the door and the narrow column (3.2, 7.65 and 10.4 m along since T-3271), the large one on the canted south-west corner's face (cant_corner), centred on it as the plate stands it, and one on the south face over the conservatory (K01's 'north' face on this east-side house). Their heads are pedimented with carved cheeks in the plate: built as K01's gabled dormer head, the carving not modelled. The iron cresting runs along the street and south curbs, the two the plate shows. T-3271: the south face's dormers re-read through the 923 Prairie photograph's camera, fitted to Hunt's plan: two, about 5.3 and 16.8 m behind the front (along 15.7 and 4.2 m, the south face measured from the rear wall), one over the conservatory's west end and one near the flank's rear, where one stood over the conservatory's middle (along 11.0 m).

roof_covering.note: The plate's mansard faces are slate laid in bands; the deck behind the curb is out of sight and is the kit's painted tin.

stair_landing_depth_m.note: The stoop's head before the door, read in the plate against the door's width.

stoop_width_m.note: The plate's stoop between its stone cheeks, about the door bay's width.

entrance_bay.note: The plate's door, numbered 1905, stands in the front's second window column from its north end, not at its middle: K01's bay 2 (K01 counts from the front's left end, which on this east-side front is its north end), its centre 6.4 m from the north corner (front_bays).

front_bays.note: The front's four window columns, from its north end: the north column, the door's, the narrow column and the library's wide window (the 1893 plate's x 220, 390, 510 and 640 px). T-3271: placed through Hunt's plan of the principal floor (its front's dimension strings, 55 ft over all), as the 923 Prairie and Daily News cameras fitted to it read them: the north column about 3.2 m from the north end, the door about 7.8 m on the plan and 7.5 m in the photograph (built 7.65 m, between them), the narrow column about 10.4 m and the wide window about 13.3 m. Before: 2.8, 6.4, 8.8 and 11.2 m, laid in proportion on the sheet's shorter front.

sash_by_storey.note: The plate's front windows, about 1.1 m wide (the columns read 1.0-1.4 m across, the narrow column narrower), their heads just under the frieze. T-3271: the storeys re-read lower through the 923 Prairie photograph's camera (storey_heights_m), the lights keep the plate's proportion to their storeys: the principal storey's 2.75 m tall from a sill 0.4 m over the floor (the plate's 3.5 m in a 5.2 m storey), the chamber storey's 2.6 m from a sill 0.3 m over its floor, which leaves K09's head and the carved crest on it 0.6 m under the frieze (the plate's 3.2 m in a 4.2 m storey reads about 2.7 m in a 4.0 m one, within 0.1 m).

basement_lights.note: The plate's basement lights under the principal windows, round-headed and barred behind the fence. T-3271 (the sign-off): cut round-headed (head: round), as the plate, the engraving and the 923 Prairie photograph (x 640, 770 and 940 px) all show them, 1.0 m across from a sill 0.5 m over grade to a crown 1.5 m up, about half a metre under the 2.0 m water table, as the plate's read through its re-solved camera; their bars are not modelled.

side_bays.note: The north flank (K01's 'south' wall on this east-side house) is out of every picture's sight: two window columns, the kit's rule.

north_bays.note: The south flank (K01's 'north' wall on this east-side house, measured from the front). T-3271, read through the 923 Prairie photograph's camera, fitted to Hunt's plan of the principal floor (data/reference_views/marshall_field_house_1905_prairie/chicagology_923_photo.json), with the render's own windows as the ruler: a window column just behind the canted corner, about 3.0 m back (built 3.1 m, its surround clear of the cut at 2.15 m), and two past the conservatory, about 14.7 and 18.8 m back, on both storeys. T-3271 (the sign-off): the photograph's two chamber windows over the conservatory, about 5.6 and 9.2 m back (x 910 and 1090 px), are laid as read windows on the chamber storey alone (the conservatory stands before the principal storey there), at the chamber's own sill and sash (6.4 m, 1.1 by 2.6 m), their sills clear over the conservatory's railed deck. Before: 7.0 and 17.5 m, the 1893 plate's column read through its camera with the heights held.

rear_bays.note: The rear is out of every picture's sight: two window columns, the kit's rule. T-3271: kept at the same places on the wall (4.55 and 13.55 m from its south end) when the main body grew 1.55 m at the south.

chimneys.note: Two stacks in the side walls; the plate shows the mansard's deck only from below and no stack clearly.

entrance_kit.note: The plate's door at the stoop's head in its stone surround, with no hood over it: the iron balcony the plate shows over the door stands at the chamber floor on its own consoles, one of the front's three balconettes (street_front_iron, T-3261), so the door hood T-3260 stood in for it at 6.0 m, about 1.4 m low, is withdrawn. The front yard to the street line is the 1904 parcel's (street_u 30.40 - 21.0 m).

boundary.note: T-3271 (the sign-off): the Daily News negative DN-0003324, c. 1905 and the picture nearest the 1904 scene, shows a tall iron picket fence on a stone curb along the street line and round the south yard: close-set pickets, each spear-topped, standing nearly to the house's water table (about 2 m), on cast-iron posts. Built as K11's spear fence on its curb, its top rail raised to 1.75 m over the curb (fence_rail_top_m) so its spears stand about 1.95 m, its gates raised with it and hung on iron posts 2.15 m high; the pickets keep the kit's 0.125 m centres, as close-set as the negative's read. Before: the 1893 plate's cast-iron scroll fence (K11's scroll-band), which the 923 Prairie photograph and the engraving show too; it is the fence of those pictures' dates, replaced by c. 1905, and the negative is followed for 1904 (an inference: the replacement's year is not read). The line stands 9.2 m before the front, just inside the parcel's street line (9.4 m); the lot's sides are the parcel's (data/street_grid/1904.json prairie_1905).

windows.why_not_ordinary: the conservatory's basement lights on its stone base, as the front's under the principal windows

bays.note: The south flank's conservatory: the 1911 sheet's bulge off the south wall between about 7 and 16 m behind the front, 'Greenhouse' written at the front's bay, and the plate's curved glasshouse on a stone base with a balcony over it, at x 955-1180 px. Built as K08's bowed bay over the basement: 8.4 m on its chord and 2.7 m out (the sheet's bulge reaches about 3.6 m off the wall; K08 holds a bow's facets to its radius). T-1905: the bow is the glasshouse's stone base only, a storey high in the house's stone with its basement light, decked flat at the principal floor, 2.0 m over grade since T-3271 (2.4 m before); the glass that stands on it, a ring of tall lights under a curved glass roof, is its own record on the K13 kit (data/structures/marshall_field_house_1905_prairie_conservatory.json, L-field-1905-conservatory-1905). The railed deck the plate shows on its roof is the conservatory record's (T-3270). T-3271: centred 9.0 m behind the front (12.0 m before): through the 923 Prairie photograph's camera, fitted to Hunt's plan, the glass runs from about 4.5 to 13.5 m back, so the 8.4 m chord stands 4.8-13.2 m, within 0.3 m of both ends; Hunt's south-flank dimension string 11 ft 0 in, 37 ft 4 in from the front (3.35 m, then 11.4 m) brackets the same stretch.

cant_corner.note: The plate cuts the house's south-west corner (K01's 'north' on this east-side house) on a broad canted face square to the corner, blank brick in both storeys between light stone strips, the bracketed cornice and the slated mansard carried round it and the largest dormer standing over it (x 683-900 px). T-3271: Hunt's plan of the principal floor draws the octagonal library's diagonal here, 6 ft 3 in (1.9 m) back each way, and the 923 Prairie photograph's camera reads the cut about 2.4 m along the front and 1.9 m along the flank; K01's cut is one length both ways, so it is built 2.15 m, within 0.3 m of both readings (it was 3.2 m, the 1893 plate's camera's reading with its heights held). The 1911 sheet draws this corner square: at its 50-foot scale a cut this size could be drawn either way, and the plate and the plan are followed (L-k01-field-1905-cant-3261). T-3271 (the sign-off): the face's brick is framed at both its angles by light stone strips from the water table to the frieze's foot, as the 923 Prairie photograph and the Daily News negative show them and the plate draws them; built as two dressed bands 0.3 m wide, 0.03 m proud, from 2.0 to 9.6 m (strips). Their width is read off the photographs at about a pier's breadth; their projection is not read and is the kit's.

rear_wings.note: The 1911 sheet's rear rectangle behind the main body's south part (u -2.5 to 0, v 4.75 to 15.25; since T-3271 laid the front's extra 1.55 m at the south it stops that much short of the main body's south wall, where the sheet's trace leaves it, and its storeys are lowered with the house's, 1.2 m under the main wall head as before), two storeys under a deck below the main cornice (the bracketed cornice runs on along the main rear wall over it), as the draft fitted its plan. The sheet's two-storey range off the north flank's rear (u -2.5 to 4.25, v -4.5 to 0) stands beside the main body rather than behind it, which K01's rear wings do not take: it is not built here and is open for T-3261. No picture shows the rear: the wing's heights, roof and windows are the kit's (reconstructed inside an inferred plan).

yard.note: K14's yard: a flagged walk from the stoop to the street gate and a cinder service walk, the kit's rule; no picture shows the walk's surface.

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '3S.B. brick dwelling (D)'. Carried to 1904 on the T-1841 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

The 1800 Prairie lot and the Glessner House footprint (stone, courtyard plan) as of 1911, and every Prairie- and Calumet-facing footprint from 18th to 20th Street
Its own printed Scale of Feet

A construction date for any building it draws
Elevations, grades, curb heights or fill depths -- no Sanborn sheet carries a level
Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
The lake edge beyond the stretch the sheet actually inks: the pen line stops while the tracks run on

research_note: Refined from the district draft (T-2330) in place by T-3260 (piece 1 of T-1904), under the draft's own id, as a K01 brick Second Empire house read off the 1893 Pictorial Chicago plate of Marshall Field's residence (rand_mcnally_pictorial_chicago_1893_field) against the 1911 sheet's plan (s28fp-1905-b1): two storeys of brick over a raised stone basement under a bracketed cornice and a tall slated mansard with dormers and an iron cresting; the front's door in its second window column from the north; the south flank's curved conservatory; the sheet's rear wing and north range; the scroll-pattern iron fence. The plate's camera and match record are in data/reference_views/marshall_field_house_1905_prairie/; what is still open (the canted south-west corner, the conservatory's glass roof and balcony, the iron balconies, the carved dormer and window heads) belongs to T-3261. Liberty L-k01-1905-field-3260.
